standard_prerequisites.name: There is a canonical map Pi(F)_x -> F_x left inverse to F_x -> Pi(F)_x, as described in the pointwise-product-stalk example
Sections of F# are families satisfying property (*): locally they are represented by genuine sections of F
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the local representative used for surjectivity.

core_obligations: Injective: the composite F_x -> Pi(F)_x -> F_x is the identity by the canonical left inverse (proof lines 1788-1793), so F_x -> F#_x is injective (proof lines 1788-1790). Surjective: take a class in F#_x represented by (U, s) with s in F#(U) (proof lines 1794-1798). By property (*) for s there are V subset U containing x and sigma in F(V) whose image in Pi(F)(V) is s|_V (proof lines 1798-1801). The class of (V, sigma) in F_x maps to the original class in F#_x (proof lines 1801-1803). Hence F_x = F#_x (proof lines 1786-1803).
proof_roadmap: Prove injectivity via the canonical left inverse of the stalk map to Pi(F)_x (proof lines 1788-1793).
Prove surjectivity by extracting a genuine section of F representing the class locally (proof lines 1794-1803).
